regla: English often says _I can see, I can hear, I can smell, I can feel_. Spanish usually drops poder and uses the plain present: veo, oigo, huelo, siento. Poder is for real ability or possibility.

bloques.texto: With the senses, English likes _can_: _I **can** see the island_. Spanish just says what you perceive: **Veo la isla**.
Questions too: _Can you hear me?_ = **¿Me oyes?** or **¿Me escuchas?**
Use **poder** only when the point is the **ability** or what's stopping it: **No puedo ver sin lentes** (_I can't see without glasses_), **Desde aquí no se puede ver el mar** (_the view is blocked_).
Quick test: if _can_ adds nothing in English (_I can smell coffee_ = _I smell coffee_), drop **poder** in Spanish.

lista.es: ==Veo== las islas Coronado desde la playa.
lista.en: I can see the Coronado Islands from the beach.
Can you hear me? It's really noisy.
I can smell adobada tacos. (lit. _It smells of adobada tacos._)

lista.es: ==Siento== el viento frío en la cara.
lista.en: I can feel the cold wind on my face.
Can you see that wave? It's a big one.
I can't hear anything with my headphones on.

lista.es: Sin lentes no ==puedo ver== el pizarrón.
lista.en: Without glasses I can't see the board. (ability)
I can hear the neighbors' music.

bloques.texto: **Puedo ver**, **¿puedes oírme?** and **puedo oler** aren't wrong, but they sound translated. Spanish usually drops **poder**: **Veo la playa desde mi casa.** **¿Me oyes?** **Huelo el café.**

lista.nota: oler: o > hue in the stressed forms.

lista.texto: Feeling with the body or heart: [[5775|sentir]], and [[7054|sentir vs sentirse]].

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I can hear the sea._
lista.r: Oigo el mar. / Escucho el mar.

lista.p: In Spanish: _Can you see the mountain?_
In Spanish: _I can smell something burning._
lista.r: Huelo algo quemado. / Huele a quemado.
